walkthroughs.body_html:
Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5°.

When the UK tilts towards the Sun: longer days, higher Sun, more heat - summer.

When the UK tilts away from the Sun: shorter days, lower Sun, less heat - winter.

Seasons aren't because Earth gets closer or further - it's the tilt!

Solar eclipse: Moon passes between Earth and Sun. Moon's shadow falls on Earth - sky goes dark in daytime.

Lunar eclipse: Earth passes between Sun and Moon. Earth's shadow falls on the Moon - it can look reddish.

Eclipses are rare because the Moon's orbit is slightly tilted.

Gravity is the force that holds everything in space together.

The Sun's gravity keeps planets in orbit. Earth's gravity keeps the Moon orbiting us, and satellites zooming around at 28,000 km/h.

Bigger mass = stronger gravity. That's why Jupiter has stronger gravity than Earth.

mcqs.q: What is required to induce an emf in a coil using a magnet?
options: Velocity is always conserved in any collision.
A changing magnetic flux linkage through the coil — the magnet (or coil) must be moving or the field must be changing.
A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.
Just having a magnet near the coil induces an emf, even when both are stationary.

mcqs.q: In a collision between two objects, what quantity is always conserved (in a closed system)?
options: Velocity is always conserved in any collision.
Total momentum is always conserved; kinetic energy is only conserved in elastic collisions.
Kinetic energy is always conserved in collisions because energy is conserved.
A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.
Velocity is always conserved in any collision.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.
